title: feat(app-shell): the flow designer shows a connector action's description and offers its output references (objectui#11028)
body:
Fixes #11028
Clause-②: no

## What an author now sees

- **The action picker shows each action's `description` beside its label.** A `connector_action` node's Action picker (a native `datalist`) now reads `Post Message (chat.postMessage) — Post a message to a channel`. An action that authors no description shows its label alone.
- **Nodes and edges downstream of a `connector_action` node offer its output.** The variable picker offers one `nodeId.key` reference for each top-level `properties` key of the chosen action's `outputSchema`. The engine stores each top-level key of the handler's result the same way. The inline "not in scope" note in the node and edge inspectors stops flagging those references.
- **Keys are never guessed.** An action with no `outputSchema`, a schema with no top-level `properties`, a `properties` that is not an object, or a node whose connector and action are not both chosen offers no references.

This is the objectui half of the action half of objectstack-ai/objectstack#20287. No trigger work. objectstack, the spec and the served descriptor are unchanged.

## Where it landed and why there

Everything is in `packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/`, the claimed surface.

- `FlowReferenceField.tsx`: the combobox `Option` had no secondary-text slot (measured: `{ value, label }`). It gains `hint`, the same name `InspectorComboField` uses for its muted suffix. `connectorActionsToOptions` fills it from the action's `description` when that is a non-blank string. The `datalist` option renders the label, then ` — `, then the hint. The descriptor carries `description` as a plain string (`ConnectorActionDescriptor.description` and `ConnectorActionSchema.description` are both `string`), so there is no locale map to resolve. A non-string value adds no hint.
- `flow-scope.ts`: `nodeOutputRefs` gains a `connector_action` branch modelled on the `approval` branch. The action's `outputSchema` lives in the served registry, not on the node, so `nodeOutputRefs(node, connectors?)` and `resolveFlowScope(draft, nodeId, locale?, connectors?)` take the already-fetched registry as an optional last argument. Two new pure helpers are unit-pinned. `connectorActionOutputSchema` is the output twin of `connectorActionInputSchema` and tolerates the same misses. `connectorActionOutputKeys` returns the top-level `properties` keys or nothing. The connector and action are read from `connectorConfig.connectorId` and `connectorConfig.actionId`, where the pickers write them. `hasCommittedConnectorAction(draft)` gates the registry read.
- The plumbing: `FlowNodeInspector` already read the registry through `useConnectorRegistry`, but only for the selected node's own input form. Its gate widens to "this node's pair OR any committed connector action in the flow", so one read serves both consumers, and the same array is handed to `useFlowScope`. `FlowEdgeInspector` had no read; it gains one behind the same gate. `useFlowScope` takes the registry as an optional fourth argument. A flow with no committed connector action never fetches for scope (pinned).

Why not have `useFlowScope` fetch for itself: in the node inspector that would be a second read of an endpoint the inspector already reads. The PM's suggested route was to reuse an existing fetch where one exists.

## Evidence (all at `c7f67b24c` unless stated)

- **Tests.** `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/app-shell/src/views/metadata-admin/inspectors/` plus the seven test files outside it that import the touched modules (`previews/flow-expr-problems.test.ts`, `previews/flow-problems.test.ts`, `previews/FlowCanvas.test.tsx`, `previews/previewStrings.i18n-10848.test.tsx`, `ActionParam.one-authority.test.ts`, `flowNodePaletteI18n.test.ts`, `scripts/__tests__/spec-symbol-ledger-app-shell-7265.test.ts`): **Test Files 118 passed (118), Tests 1662 passed, 1 skipped (1663)**.
- **Type-check.** First `pnpm turbo run build --filter='@object-ui/app-shell^...' --concurrency=2` built the dependency closure (28 tasks). Without that build the type-check cannot resolve `@object-ui/*`, so a type-check on a fresh worktree reads red for a reason unrelated to this change. Then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` (`tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`) exited 0. `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --listFilesOnly` lists all four touched test files, and the test project did catch a fixture typing slip in the new inspector test before its fix commit.
- **Lint, narrowed and shown to exclude nothing.**
  - What is checked: every changed `.ts`/`.tsx` file, all inside `eslint.config.js`'s `files: ['**/*.{ts,tsx}']` blocks.
  - `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the 9 changed files reports 9 files, 0 errors and 16 warnings.
  - The same five source files at the base `51c294958` give identical per-file warning counts (2 / 4 / 10 / 0 / 0). All 16 warnings predate this change, and the new test files have none.
  - Untouched files cannot change verdict: `eslint.config.js` sets no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService` (no type-aware linting), and no custom rule under `eslint-rules/` reads the filesystem, so this diff cannot move a rule's verdict on any other file. The repo-wide `pnpm lint` is CI's.
- **Gates.** These exited 0 at `c7f67b24c`:
  - `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs`, `check-changeset-claims.mjs`, `check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, `check-changeset-overwrite.mjs`, `check-changeset-fixed.mjs`
  - `check-control-bytes.mjs`, `check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs`
  - `check-vi-mock-specifiers.mjs`, `check-vi-mock-inherit.mjs`, `check-vi-mock-override-shape.mjs`, `check-test-path-roots.mjs`
  - `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` over the changed paths: NOT GOVERNED

  These also exited 0, before the last test-only commit: `pnpm check:spec-symbols`, `check:designer-field-key-parity`, `check:handler-key-reads`, `check:unreferenced-sources`, `check:i18n-keys` (no pack key added) and `check:action-forward-parity`.
- **Ablations.** Each leg mutated one committed file through `ablation-replace.mjs`, which requires the anchor to hit and proves the restore by blob hash against HEAD. The inspector tests import sources directly, so no `dist` is involved. Each leg ran the four touched test files:
  - A: the branch stops adding keys (`flow-scope.ts`). 4 failed: the two-refs pin, the downstream-scope pin, and the node and edge inspector positives. The lit controls stayed green.
  - B: `FlowNodeInspector` stops handing the registry to the scope. 1 failed: the node inspector positive.
  - C: `FlowEdgeInspector` stops handing it. 1 failed: the edge inspector positive.
  - D: the `datalist` renders the label only. The first attempt was refused by the tool because the replacement text already occurred, so no mutation ran and it gives no reading. The rerun with a distinct replacement: 2 failed, both picker render pins.
  - E: `connectorActionsToOptions` sets no hint. 3 failed: the hint unit pin and both render pins.
  - Every leg restored to HEAD with `git diff HEAD` empty.

## Acceptance notes

These are observations, not in this diff:

1. **The Problems panel still flags a connector action's output references.** `flowExpressionProblems` (`previews/flow-expr-problems.ts`) is a pure pass that calls `resolveFlowScope(draft, nodeId)` with no registry. A guard downstream of a committed connector action that reads `post.ok` is therefore reported as "`post` is not a reference in scope at this step", while the inspectors now judge it in scope. This was measured by a throwaway probe against that function (not committed). Before this change both surfaces flagged it. Closing it means handing the registry to `flowProblems` from the component that renders the panel, which is a new read site outside this card's surface. It is reported to the seat, not fixed here.
2. **An edge guard never sees its own source node's outputs.** Both the edge inspector and the Problems panel resolve an edge's scope at `resolveFlowScope(draft, edge.source)`, which excludes the source node's own outputs. The engine evaluates out-edge guards after it writes that node's `output` back. So a guard on the edge right after a `get_record` that reads its `outputVariable` is flagged, as is `approvalNodeId.decision` after an approval, and now `post.ok` right after a connector node. The throwaway probe measured the `get_record` case flagged, and the same guard one node further downstream clean. This is pre-existing for every node type and not in this diff.
3. `connectorActionOutputSchema` and `connectorActionInputSchema` repeat the same eight-line registry lookup. They were kept apart because `connector-input-fields.ts` imports React and the palette module, and `flow-scope.ts` stays free of both.
